s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic photosensitive eruption with skin and possible muscle involvement
salient_findings: Photosensitive eruption involving face, neck, trunk, and extremities
Poikiloderma and erythematous papules on extensor joints
Nailfold changes with dilated capillary loops and capillary dropout
key_facts: Age of onset: 8 years
Duration of symptoms: 6 years
Previous treatments included systemic steroids, hydroxychloroquine, methotrexate, and others with minimal improvement
Clinical examination revealed violaceous erythema on forehead and midface
Diffuse poikiloderma involving upper chest, anterolateral thighs, and extensor arms
Erythematous, flat-topped papules on extensor joints of hands
Nailfold examination showed dilated capillary loops, capillary dropout, and ragged cuticles
Elevated serum IFN-β levels (8 pg/mL, normal ≤2 pg/mL)
Presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies
Radiographic evidence of myositis
Confirmatory skin biopsy performed

shortlist.label: Anti-TIF-1γ juvenile dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies and clinical features consistent with juvenile dermatomyositis

shortlist.label: Juvenile dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical examination and laboratory findings consistent with dermatomyositis, including skin and muscle involvement

shortlist.label: Systemic lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Photosensitive eruption and possible muscle involvement, although less likely given the presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies

shortlist.label: Dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical features consistent with dermatomyositis, although less specific than Anti-TIF-1γ juvenile dermatomyositis

shortlist.label: Polymyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Radiographic evidence of myositis, although less likely given the prominent skin involvement

raw.rationale: The presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies, elevated serum IFN-β levels, and clinical features such as violaceous erythema, poikiloderma, and nailfold capillary changes are consistent with this diagnosis. The patient's age of onset and duration of symptoms also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Juvenile dermatomyositis
rejected.why: While the patient's symptoms are consistent with JDM, the presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies specifically points to Anti-TIF-1γ JDM

rejected.label: Systemic lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and laboratory findings do not strongly support SLE, and the presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies is more specific to JDM

rejected.label: Dermatomyositis
rejected.why: The patient's age and clinical features suggest a juvenile form of the disease, and the presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies points to a specific subtype

rejected.label: Polymyositis
rejected.why: The patient's clinical presentation, including skin involvement, is not consistent with polymyositis, which typically presents with muscle weakness alone
